parsed.title: Packing conjecture for infinite matroid families
parsed.statement: Let $(M_k\mid k\in K)$ be a family of matroids on the same ground set $E$. A **covering** for $(M_k.Y\mid k\in K)$ is a family of independent sets whose union covers $Y$, and a **packing** is a family of pairwise disjoint spanning sets. **Packing conjecture.** The family $(M_k\mid k\in K)$ has a packing if and only if, for every $Y\subseteq E$, whenever $(M_k.Y\mid k\in K)$ has a covering, it also has a packing. This condition is designed as an infinite analogue of the finite base packing theorem and is stated to characterize when a packing exists.
parsed.source_name: Nathan Bowler and Johannes Carmesin, “Matroid intersection, base packing and base covering for infinite matroids”, arXiv:1202.3409 (2012).

parsed.title: A small-sumset counting conjecture
parsed.statement:
For positive integers $n$, let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and for a finite set $S$ write $S+S=\{a+b:a,b\in S\}$. **Small-sumset counting conjecture.** For every $\delta>0$, there exists $C>0$ such that, whenever $m\geq C\sqrt{N}$ and $m\geq C\log n$, there are at most

$$
2^{\delta m}{N/2\choose m}
$$

sets $S\subset[n]$ with $|S|=m$ and $|S+S|\leq N$. The conjecture would strengthen the bounds on the number of sets with small sumset needed in the paper, extending the preceding theorem to the regime relevant to dense sum-free-set arguments. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.
parsed.source_name: Noga Alon, József Balogh, Robert Morris and Wojciech Samotij, “A refinement of the Cameron-Erdős Conjecture”, arXiv:1202.5200 (2012).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.5200

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2012). “This conjecture was confirmed by Green and, independently, by Sapozhenko.”

parsed.title: Monotonicity conjecture for ordinarization-number counts
parsed.statement:
A **numerical semigroup** is a cofinite additive submonoid of ${\mathbb N}_0$. For $g,r\in{\mathbb N}_0$, let $n_{g,r}$ be the number of numerical semigroups of genus $g$ and ordinarization number $r$; for $r>\lfloor g/2\rfloor$, set $n_{g,r}=0$.

**Ordinarization-count monotonicity conjecture.** For every $g,r\in{\mathbb N}_0$,

$$
n_{g,r}\leq n_{g+1,r}.
$$

Computations for $g\leq49$ showed that the counts for each ordinarization number increase with genus or remain unchanged. The conjecture is the precise fixed-depth formulation of the monotonicity claim for the trees ${\mathscr T}_g$ and ${\mathscr T}_{g+1}$.
parsed.source_name: Maria Bras-Amorós, “Ordinarization Transform of a Numerical Semigroup and Semigroups with a Large Number of Intervals”, arXiv:1203.5000 (2012).

parsed.title: Independence of multispins in rooted forests of Cartesian products of complete graphs
parsed.statement: Let $G=(U,A)$ be a weighted digraph, let $K_p$ be the complete graph with vertex set $[p]$, and let $H=G\times K_p$ be their Cartesian product. A rooted forest of $H$ has a **$G$-projection** if it records the number of $a$-arcs for every $a\in A$ and the number of vertical arcs at every $u\in U$. For a rooted forest $F$ and $u\in U$, let $\sigma_u$ denote the multiset of spins of the vertical arcs of $F$ at $u$. Given a rooted forest $F_0$ of $H$, choose $F$ uniformly among rooted forests of $H$ having the same $G$-projection as $F_0$. **Independence of multispins.** The multispins $(\sigma_u)_{u\in U}$ of $F$ at the different vertices of $G$ are independent.

parsed.title: The local rigidity conjecture for graphs with infinite neighbourhood differences
parsed.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be an infinite graph, and write $\Gamma(x)$ for the neighbourhood of a vertex $x$. Assume that for every pair of distinct vertices $x,y$,

$$
\Gamma(x)\mathbin{\triangle}\Gamma(y)
$$

is infinite. A graph is **locally rigid** when its automorphism group acts locally rigidly on its vertex set. **Graph local rigidity conjecture.** $\Gamma$ is locally rigid. The statement is described as a conjectural strengthening of results in the paper and as a special case of a stronger conjecture from earlier work; it remains open in the source.

parsed.title: Factorial growth conjecture for hatted pattern-avoiding permutations
parsed.statement:
Let $\tau$ be a permutation pattern and let $\hat\tau_{(i)}$ denote the hatted pattern obtained by placing a hat over the $i$th entry of $\tau$. Write $S_n(\hat\tau_{(i)})$ for the permutations of length $n$ avoiding this hatted pattern.

**Factorial growth conjecture.** The growth rate of $|S_n(\hat\tau_{(i)})|$ is factorial for every hatted pattern $\hat\tau_{(i)}$.

This conjecture proposes that all hatted pattern-avoidance classes have factorial growth. The paper notes that the analogous Wilf–Stanley conjecture fails for hatted patterns, while the displayed construction establishes a factorial lower bound in the considered setting; the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied source.
parsed.source_name: Phan Thuan Do, Dominique Rossin and Thi Thu Huong Tran, “Combinatorial bijections from hatted avoiding permutations in S_n(132) to generalized Dyck and Motzkin paths”, arXiv:1208.1075 (2012).

parsed.title: Nonzero equivalence conjecture for negative scoring positions
parsed.statement:
Let $
\mathcal{PT}_{-x}$ be the set of scoring-play game positions in which every node has value $x>0$ and the initial score is $0$. Write $G\cong 0$ for equivalence to the zero game and $G=0$ for equality with the zero game. **Nonzero equivalence conjecture.** For all $G\in\mathcal{PT}_{-x}$, if $G\not\cong 0$ then $G\neq 0$. This follows a discussion of whether scoring games can behave like normal-play games, but the source provides no argument resolving the stated implication.

parsed.title: The primitive sigma-LFSR enumeration conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers. A primitive $c3$-LFSR of order $n$ over ${\mathbb F}_{q^m}$ is a word-oriented feedback shift register whose associated sequence has maximal possible period. **Primitive $c3$-LFSR enumeration conjecture.** The number of primitive $c3$-LFSRs of order $n$ over ${\mathbb F}_{q^m}$ is

$$
\frac{\phi(q^{mn}-1)}{mn} \, q^{m(m-1)(n-1)} \prod_{i=1}^{m-1}(q^m-q^i).
$$

This conjecture extends a conjecture proposed in the binary case to arbitrary finite fields. The paper presents it as a conjecture motivating its study, while the supplied status information leaves it open.

parsed.title: The f-vector comparison conjecture for order and chain polytopes
parsed.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset with $|P|=d>1$. The **order polytope** ${\mathcal O}(P)$ and **chain polytope** ${\mathcal C}(P)$ are the polytopes associated with $P$, and write their $f$-vectors as

$$
f({\mathcal O}(P))=(f_0,f_1,\ldots,f_{d-1}),\qquad f({\mathcal C}(P))=(f'_0,f'_1,\ldots,f'_{d-1}).
$$

**The f-vector comparison conjecture.** One has $f_i\leq f'_i$ for all $1\leq i\leq d-1$. Moreover, if $f_i=f'_i$ for some $1\leq i\leq d-1$, then ${\mathcal O}(P)$ and ${\mathcal C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent.

The claim compares the face numbers of the two naturally associated polytopes. The supplied text does not give evidence that this statement has been resolved, so its status remains open.
parsed.source_name: Takayuki Hibi and Nan Li, “Unimodular equivalence of order and chain polytopes”, arXiv:1208.4029 (2012).

parsed.title: The strong virtual periodicity conjecture for maximal coclass trees
parsed.statement:
Let $r\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $K$ be an arbitrary field. Let $\mathcal T$ be a maximal coclass tree in $\mathcal G_{r,K}$ with maximal infinite path $A_1\to A_2\to\cdots$. Write $\overline{\mathcal T}(A)$ for the unlabelled rooted tree at $A$. **Strong virtual periodicity conjecture.** There exist positive integers $l$ and $k$, a graph isomorphism

$$
\mu:\overline{\mathcal T}(A_l)\longrightarrow\overline{\mathcal T}(A_{l+k}),
$$

and, for every vertex $B\in\mathcal T(A_l)\setminus\mathcal T(A_{l+k})$, a rational polynomial $f_B$ such that the label of $\mu^i(B)$ equals $f_B(i)$. This strengthens weak virtual periodicity by requiring eventual polynomial behaviour of labels; its resolution is not supplied here.

parsed.title: The fixed-collinearity general-position colouring conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane with at most $\ell$ collinear. A colouring of $P$ has each colour class in general position when no colour class contains three collinear points. **Fixed-collinearity colouring conjecture.** For all fixed $\ell\geqslant3$, every such set $P$ can be coloured with $O_{\ell}(\operatorname{polylog}(n))$ colours such that each colour class is in general position.

The source states that this colouring conjecture is equivalent to the fixed-collinearity general position subset conjecture by an argument similar to the preceding proposition. The corresponding problem remains open; the density Hales–Jewett construction supplies point sets with sublinear upper bounds.

parsed.title: Albert–Atkinson conjecture on layered patterns maximizing avoidance
parsed.statement:
Let $S_n(q)$ denote the number of permutations of length $n$ that avoid a pattern $q$. A pattern is **layered** if it consists of decreasing subsequences whose entries increase from one layer to the next. Let $q$ be a non-layered pattern of length $k$, and let $Q$ be a layered pattern of length $k$. **Layered-pattern maximality conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$,

$$
S_n(q)\leq S_n(Q).
$$

If true, bounds for layered patterns would give bounds for all patterns of the same length. Numerical evidence supports the conjecture, but the general assertion remains open.
parsed.source_name: Miklos Bona, “On the Best Upper Bound for Permutations Avoiding A Pattern of a Given Length”, arXiv:1209.2404 (2012).

parsed.title: The free-extension characterization of algebraic extensions
parsed.statement:
Let $H\leq J$ be subgroups of a free group $\mathbf{F}$. Let $\mathbf{F}'$ be a free extension of $\mathbf{F}$, meaning that $\mathbf{F}\leq\mathbf{F}'$ and $\mathbf{F}'$ is free, and let $X$ be a basis of $\mathbf{F}'$. Write $H\leq_{{\scriptscriptstyle \overset{\twoheadrightarrow}{X}}}J$ when the canonical morphism from the Stallings core graph $\Gamma_X(H)$ to $\Gamma_X(J)$ is onto. **Modified algebraic-extension conjecture.** Then

$$
H\leq_{alg}J\quad\text{if and only if}\quad H\leq_{{\scriptscriptstyle \overset{\twoheadrightarrow}{X}}}J
$$

for every free extension $\mathbf{F}'$ of $\mathbf{F}$ and every basis $X$ of $\mathbf{F}'$. This proposed modification is presented after the original conjecture is shown to fail, and the source gives no resolution of it.

parsed.title: Faber–Krahn conjecture for unicyclic degree sequences
parsed.statement:
Let $\pi=(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{k-1},1,\ldots,1)$ be a graphic unicyclic degree sequence with $2\le d_0\le d_1\le\ldots\le d_{k-1}$ and $d_k=\ldots=d_{n-1}=1$. Let $\mathcal{U}_{\pi}$ denote the class of unicyclic graphs with degree sequence $\pi$, let $U_{\pi,B}^*$ be the specified extremal graph, and let $\lambda^D(G)$ denote the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $G$. **Faber–Krahn conjecture.** For every $G\in\mathcal{U}_{\pi}$,

$$
\lambda^D(G)\ge\lambda^D(U_{\pi,B}^*)
$$

with equality if and only if $G=U_{\pi,B}^*$. Equivalently, $U_{\pi,B}^*$ is the unique graph with the Faber–Krahn property in $\mathcal{U}_{\pi}$. The preceding theorem establishes this assertion when $d_0\ge3$; the conjecture concerns the remaining case $d_0=2$.
parsed.source_name: Xiao-Dong Zhang, “Extremal Graph Theory for Degree Sequences”, arXiv:1510.01903 (2015).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1201.0455](https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.0455).

parsed.title: White's conjecture on equivalence of matroid basis sequences
parsed.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid, and let

$$
\mathcal{X}=(X_1,\dots,X_m),\qquad \mathcal{Y}=(Y_1,\dots,Y_m)
$$

be sequences of bases of $M$ of the same length. Two basis sequences are **equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by a composition of symmetric exchanges between two sequence positions. They are **compatible** if, for every ground-set element $s$, it occurs equally many times in the two sequences:

$$
\left|\{i:s\in X_i,\ 1\leq i\leq m\}\right|=\left|\{i:s\in Y_i,\ 1\leq i\leq m\}\right|.
$$

**White's conjecture.** The sequences $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ are equivalent if and only if they are compatible.
Compatibility is evidently necessary, and the conjecture is connected with toric ideals, Gröbner bases, and the connectivity of basis-pair graphs. It remains open even for sequences of length two.
parsed.source_name: Kristóf Bérczi and Tamás Schwarcz, “Exchange distance of basis pairs in split matroids”, arXiv:2203.01779 (2022).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01779

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2022). “Despite being the center of attention not only in combinatorial optimization but also in algebra due to its connection to toric ideals and Gröbner bases , White's conjecture remains open even for sequences of length two.”

parsed.title: Three-translate linear stability conjecture for finite subsets of the integers
parsed.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be finite subsets of $\mathbb{Z}$ of equal size $n$. For $b_1,b_2,b_3\in B$, write $A+\{b_1,b_2,b_3\}=\{a+b_i:a\in A,\,i\in\{1,2,3\}\}$. For finite sets $X,Y$, write $X\mathbin{\Delta}Y$ for their symmetric difference.

**Three-translate linear stability conjecture.** For every $\delta>0$ there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, if

$$
|A+\{b_1,b_2,b_3\}|\leqslant (2+\varepsilon)n-1
$$

for every $b_1,b_2,b_3\in B$, then there exist arithmetic progressions $P,Q$ in $\mathbb{Z}$ with the same common difference such that

$$
B\subset Q\qquad\text{and}\qquad |A\mathbin{\Delta}P|,\ |B\mathbin{\Delta}Q|\leqslant\delta n.
$$

This is the proposed three-translate analogue of the paper's inverse theorem for four translates. The source presents this weaker stability form as conjectural, while noting that a stronger version is also expected.
parsed.source_name: Bela Bollobas, Imre Leader and Marius Tiba, “A strengthening of Freiman's 3k-4 theorem”, arXiv:2204.09816 (2022).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.09816

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

parsed.title: Duality invariance of matroid p-characteristic sets
parsed.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid and let $M^*$ be its dual. Write $4\chi_M4$ for the p-characteristic set of $M$.

**Duality conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{M^*}=\chi_M.
$$

This would extend the equality already known for prime-power characteristics, where representability of a matroid over a finite field is equivalent to representability of its dual over the same field. The conjecture asks whether the corresponding equality holds for all integers $v\ge 2$; the construction of a $4\mathrm{VOA}(M^*,v)4$ from a $4\mathrm{VOA}(M,v)4$ is not established in the supplied text.
parsed.source_name: Qi Chen, Minquan Cheng and Baoming Bai, “Matroidal Entropy Functions: Constructions, Characterizations and Representations”, arXiv:2306.17041 (2024).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1203.1255](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.1255).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17041

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).
